description: A color's invoiced amount is the total `product_quantity` on invoice lines for products of that color.

d.request: Group invoice line items by product color (with NULL/missing color as a separate group), sum product_quantity for each color to calculate invoiced amount, determine each color's percentage share of total invoiced quantity, identify colors with invoiced amount exceeding the average per color, and return one row containing the average invoiced amount of those above-average colors, their average share percentage, and their average exceeding amount above the per-color average.
d.sql:
WITH color_summary AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(p.product_color, 'NULL') AS product_color,
    SUM(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4))) AS invoiced_amount,
    SUM(SUM(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4)))) OVER () AS total_quantity
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  LEFT JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY COALESCE(p.product_color, 'NULL')
),
color_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    product_color,
    invoiced_amount,
    (invoiced_amount / total_quantity) * 100 AS share_percentage,
    AVG(invoiced_amount) OVER () AS avg_invoiced_amount
  FROM color_summary
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT 
    product_color,
    invoiced_amount,
    share_percentage,
    invoiced_amount - avg_invoiced_amount AS exceeding_amount
  FROM color_stats
  WHERE invoiced_amount > avg_invoiced_amount
)
SELECT 
  AVG(invoiced_amount) AS avg_invoiced_amount_above_average,
  AVG(share_percentage) AS avg_share_percentage,
  AVG(exceeding_amount) AS avg_exceeding_amount
FROM above_average

c.request: How much of each product color was invoiced? Products with no color count as their own group. Work out each color's share of the total invoiced. Look at the colors whose invoiced amount is above the average per color. For those colors, give one row with their average invoiced amount, their average share, and how far above the per-color average they are on average. Don't round anything. A color's invoiced amount is the total `product_quantity` on invoice lines for products of that color.
c.sql: WITH color_totals AS (SELECT COALESCE(p.product_color, 'No Color') as color, SUM(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4))) as invoiced_amount FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY COALESCE(p.product_color, 'No Color')), grand_total AS (SELECT SUM(invoiced_amount) as total_invoiced FROM color_totals), color_with_share AS (SELECT ct.color, ct.invoiced_amount, ct.invoiced_amount / gt.total_invoiced as share FROM color_totals ct CROSS JOIN grand_total gt), color_avg AS (SELECT AVG(invoiced_amount) as avg_per_color FROM color_totals), above_average_colors AS (SELECT cws.color, cws.invoiced_amount, cws.share, (cws.invoiced_amount - ca.avg_per_color) as above_average_amount FROM color_with_share cws CROSS JOIN color_avg ca WHERE cws.invoiced_amount > ca.avg_per_color) SELECT AVG(invoiced_amount) as avg_invoiced_amount, AVG(share) as avg_share, AVG(above_average_amount) as avg_above_average FROM above_average_colors

b.request: For each product color (treating NULL colors as a separate group), sum the `product_quantity` from `Invoice_Line_Items` as the invoiced amount per color; identify colors whose total invoiced amount exceeds the average invoiced amount across all colors; return one row with the average invoiced amount of those above-average colors, the average share of total invoiced quantity for those colors, and the average amount by which those colors exceed the per-color average invoiced amount.
b.sql: WITH color_totals AS (SELECT COALESCE(product_color, 'NULL') as color, SUM(CAST(product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4))) as total_invoiced FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY COALESCE(product_color, 'NULL')), stats AS (SELECT AVG(total_invoiced) as avg_invoiced, SUM(total_invoiced) as overall_total FROM color_totals), above_average_colors AS (SELECT ct.total_invoiced, ct.total_invoiced / s.overall_total as share, ct.total_invoiced - s.avg_invoiced as excess FROM color_totals ct CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE ct.total_invoiced > s.avg_invoiced) SELECT AVG(total_invoiced) as avg_invoiced_amount_above_avg_colors, AVG(share) as avg_share_of_total, AVG(excess) as avg_excess_over_average FROM above_average_colors
b.raw: For each product color (treating NULL colors as a separate group), sum the `product_quantity` from `Invoice_Line_Items` as the invoiced amount per color; identify colors whose total invoiced amount exceeds the average invoiced amount across all colors; return one row with the average invoiced amount of those above-average colors, the average share of total invoiced quantity for those colors, and the average amount by which those colors exceed the per-color average invoiced amount.

a.request: For each product color, add up the `product_quantity` (as a whole number) on invoice line items for products of that color. Products with no color count as their own group. Work out each color's share of the overall quantity. Keep the colors whose quantity is above the average quantity per color. Over those colors, give one row with the average quantity, the average share, and the average amount by which the quantity exceeds the per-color average. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH color_totals AS (SELECT p.product_color, SUM(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4))) as total_quantity FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_color), overall_stats AS (SELECT SUM(total_quantity) as overall_total, AVG(total_quantity) as avg_qty_per_color FROM color_totals), above_average AS (SELECT ct.product_color, ct.total_quantity, ct.total_quantity / os.overall_total as share, os.avg_qty_per_color, ct.total_quantity - os.avg_qty_per_color as excess FROM color_totals ct CROSS JOIN overall_stats os WHERE ct.total_quantity > os.avg_qty_per_color) SELECT AVG(total_quantity) as average_quantity, AVG(share) as average_share, AVG(excess) as average_excess FROM above_average
